sections.heading: Start Your Project with Proper Site Preparation
sections.body: Bellhouse Excavating handles site preparation across Brantford, Brant County, and surrounding areas, including stripping topsoil, rough grading, land shaping, and excavation for foundations, access routes, site servicing components, and drainage. Proper site prep sets your project up for long-term success.

sections.heading: Where This Site Prep Work Adds the Most Value
sections.subheading: Best fit for projects that need practical grading decisions, stable pads, and clear access before the next phase of construction starts.

cards.title: Raw lots that need build-ready grades
cards.body: A good fit when the site still needs stripping, rough grade correction, and usable elevations established before foundation, utility, or framing crews step in.
cards.outcome: Gets the site into a cleaner, more buildable condition instead of leaving grading and stripping spread across multiple small scopes.

cards.title: Pads, drainage shaping, and access routes
cards.body: Works well when the job needs more than surface smoothing and actually depends on stable pads, sensible water movement, and dependable route prep for trucks and machines.
cards.outcome: Supports a site that drains properly and stays workable for material delivery, concrete, and follow-on trades.

cards.title: Contractor-led site prep with material movement
cards.body: A strong fit for active projects where cut, fill, imported aggregate, and on-site material handling all need to stay aligned with schedule instead of being split between crews.
cards.outcome: Helps keep prep, grading, and haul coordination moving as one operation rather than separate call-outs.

sections.heading: Project Fit & Site Review
sections.subheading: Site preparation is strongest where equipment staging, truck access, and material movement can be planned before the next construction phase. Fit is decided by scope and access, not by property type.

items.title: Best fit: Builder and contractor site prep
items.body: Projects where stripping, grading, pad prep, and drainage all need to stay coordinated with the build schedule instead of being split across separate crews.

items.title: Especially strong fit: Rural, farm, and large-lot new builds
items.body: Properties with room for equipment access, truck staging, and material stockpiling. Barn sites, shop pads, rural residential builds, and acreage lots across Brant County are where Bellhouse's fleet works most efficiently.

items.title: Reviewed case by case: Tight access sites
items.body: Smaller residential or in-town sites may need different equipment, trucking, or spoil-handling plans. If access, utility clearance, and staging can be managed, Bellhouse can review the scope before deciding the practical approach.

items.title: Not the best fit: Landscaping and finish work
items.body: Bellhouse brings sites to rough or finish grade for the next trade. Sod, planting, retaining walls, and decorative landscape work are separate scopes.

factors.title: Site size and topsoil stripping area
factors.body: More area to strip, haul, or stockpile means more machine time and truck loads before grading can begin.

factors.title: Cut and fill volume
factors.body: Sites with significant grade changes need more material moved — either hauled off, redistributed, or imported to bring elevations to design.

factors.title: Drainage and ditching scope
factors.body: Swales, ditches, culverts, and drainage prep add scope when the site has water management challenges built into the grade.

factors.title: Imported aggregate or fill
factors.body: When the site needs granular base, fill, or imported material, truck loads, placement, and compaction all add cost.

factors.title: Access and working conditions
factors.body: Tight lots, soft ground, active adjacent construction, and utility conflicts all affect how much time and care the prep work requires.

sections.heading: What The Site Should Be Ready For After Prep
sections.subheading: Good site preparation should leave the job workable, drainable, and ready for the next trade instead of needing another round of correction.

items.title: Build-ready pads and working grades
items.body: The site is stripped, shaped, and brought to practical elevations so foundation, framing, utility, or concrete crews can move into usable ground.

items.title: Cleaner drainage and access decisions
items.body: Water movement, ditching, and route prep are handled as part of the grading plan so the site stays more stable through the construction phase.

items.title: Better coordination of cut, fill, and hauled material
items.body: Material movement stays aligned with the grading work instead of turning into separate truck calls and rework after the site is already open.

sections.heading: What Proper Site Prep Helps Prevent
sections.subheading: Site work usually gets more expensive when grading, drainage, and access are treated like cleanup instead of part of the first real phase of construction.

items.problem: Unstripped topsoil and soft spots can leave pads and access areas unstable for the crews that follow.
items.solution: Bellhouse strips organics, exposes workable subgrade, and prepares pads and routes that support the next construction phase.

items.problem: Poor grading decisions early on can create drainage trouble, ponding, and rework once the site starts taking shape.
items.solution: Rough grading, slope control, and ditching are handled with drainage in mind before the lot gets locked into the wrong elevations.

items.problem: Jobs that separate excavation, hauling, and imported material too much often lose time between phases.
items.solution: Bellhouse keeps grading, trucking, aggregate movement, and site shaping coordinated so prep work moves as one operation.

items.question: Can you prepare sites for new builds?
items.answer: Yes. Bellhouse regularly prepares sites for new homes, farm shops, barns, and agricultural buildings across Brant County. Site prep typically includes topsoil stripping, rough grading to design elevations, building pad preparation, and drainage shaping. The goal is a build-ready surface where foundation, framing, or concrete crews can step in without regrading.

items.question: Do you handle drainage as part of site prep?
items.answer: Yes. Grading for drainage is a core part of how Bellhouse approaches site preparation. That includes shaping slopes to direct water away from building pads, cutting swales and ditches, and establishing drainage paths before construction locks in the wrong elevations. On sites that need underground drainage, Bellhouse can excavate, bed pipe, place stone, and backfill as part of the grading scope.

items.question: Can you work from engineered site plans?
items.answer: Yes. Bellhouse works directly from survey drawings, engineered grading plans, and site layout documents. Laser and GPS grade control are used to match proposed elevations accurately. If plans are still in progress, a site walk and discussion of the project scope are usually enough to start the quoting process.

items.question: How long does site preparation typically take?
items.answer: Most residential or farm site prep jobs take a few days to a week depending on the lot size, topsoil depth, grade correction needed, and whether imported aggregate is required. Larger commercial or multi-pad projects may take longer. Bellhouse confirms a realistic timeline after reviewing the site, scope, and access conditions.

items.question: Do I need to remove trees or clear brush before site prep starts?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Bellhouse can handle tree and brush clearing as part of the site prep scope where equipment access allows. Stripping, grubbing, and clearing are typically done in the same mobilization as the grading work so the site moves from raw land to build-ready in one coordinated phase.
